history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 21, audited at commit dff8775 (HEAD of the main checkout, tree
45a8ebe2...). Sprint file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict. Two files,
both under lib/llm.

VERDICT: PASS.

R5 -- PROVED BY MUTATION, not by reading. The new test writes the expected prompt out
as a literal and compares with toBe, which is only meaningful if it is not secretly
comparing the constant to itself. I exported the tree to a scratch copy, changed one
character in SYSTEM_PROMPT -- "no rhetorical flourish" to "no rhetorical flourishes" --
and re-ran:

  baseline:  15 passed
  mutated:   1 failed  (SYSTEM_PROMPT ... asserts the exact register/grounding string)

So the assertion is genuinely exact and genuinely independent. That is what R5 asked
for and it is the one requirement here that could have been satisfied in appearance
only: importing the constant and asserting equality against itself would have passed
forever while protecting nothing. It does not do that. The two supporting tests -- the
old register language absent, both grounding clauses present -- are belt and braces on
top.

R3 -- I FACT-CHECKED THE EXEMPLAR, since the criterion assigns that to me by name.

  "Mars squared Neptune, and that week a labor strike shut the harbor down. Force
   meeting water rarely stays symbolic for long."

There is no falsifiable real-world claim in it. No named harbor, no named year, no
named strike or union, no date attached to the aspect. The only correspondence
asserted is Mars-as-force and Neptune-as-water, which is conventional and correct --
Mars is force and action, Neptune is the sea god and rules a water sign.

Satisfying "any real-world detail must be factually correct" by removing the surface
on which a fact could be wrong is the right move rather than a dodge, and the comment
above the prompt says so explicitly. An exemplar naming a real incident would have
been a standing hostage: correct today, and one careless edit from teaching
approximation in the single prompt where approximation is the failure mode.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET. "playful" is gone from the opening line and "Warm and a little grand. Never
  ominous." is gone from the rules. The replacement carries all four elements R1
  named, nearly verbatim: no grandeur, no rhetorical flourish, one
  placement/event/connection per sentence where possible, concrete nouns over
  adjectives. It is a replacement rather than a softening -- the old lines are not
  hedged, they are absent, and a test asserts their absence. See note 2 on the
  criterion's wording.
R2 MET, and this is the requirement the sprint file is right to call the important
  one. The grounding rule now reads "Invent no astrological data beyond what is
  supplied, and invent no detail about the events beyond what is supplied." The
  original clause is retained verbatim rather than reworded, and the new clause
  extends it rather than replacing it. The module comment states the reasoning --
  concreteness raises fabrication pressure, so the grounding is strengthened in the
  same edit -- which is the part that stops someone later trimming the sentence for
  brevity.
R3 MET. See above.
R4 MET, checked item by item rather than by reading the diff summary: TEMPERATURE is
  still 0.9, TOP_ASPECT_COUNT still 6, round2 still applied to both the position and
  aspect lines, the no-hedging rule intact, "Two to four short paragraphs" intact,
  TIMEOUT_MS unchanged. buildPrompt itself is untouched -- the diff contains no change
  to slice, toFixed, topAspects or any assembly logic.
R5 MET. See above.
No change to generate.ts, the write path, the kill switch or any UI: git diff
  --name-only returns exactly lib/llm/horoscope.ts and lib/llm/horoscope.test.ts.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 182 tests across 18 files, 3 new.
- next build exits 0.
- Built with probe values for OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and grepped
  the whole .next output: both absent.

Notes, not conditions:
1. The exemplar demonstrates concreteness without demonstrating groundedness, and
   those are the two things this sprint is trying to hold together. "a labor strike
   shut the harbor down" is specific event detail that no input supplied -- which is
   the behaviour the rule two paragraphs below forbids. The example teaches "name a
   specific event"; the rule says "invent no detail about the events beyond what is
   supplied". A model reconciles that by naming specifics from the events it is given,
   which is the wanted outcome, but the example does not show it doing so.
   An exemplar framed as operating on supplied event text -- given "1919: dockworkers
   struck", write this -- would model both halves at once, and would make the register
   and the grounding rule teach the same lesson instead of adjacent ones.
   I am not making this a condition. R3 asks for factual correctness and gets it,
   prompt design is a judgement rather than a defect, and GroundTruth's second
   criterion tests the actual outcome on exactly the path where fabrication would show
   first. But this sprint names "concreteness bought with fabrication" as its central
   risk, and the exemplar is the one place in the diff that pulls toward it.
2. R1's acceptance criterion says "the three register-setting elements are gone". Read
   literally that fails, because Context names the paragraph allowance as the third and
   R4 explicitly requires the paragraph count to stay. Read against R1's own text --
   which asks for two removals, not three -- the implementation is exactly right, and
   that is how I audited it. This is the sixth instance of a criterion worded slightly
   wider or narrower than the requirement it serves (Sprints 4, 15, 19, 20, 22 and now
   21). Individually harmless every time; collectively it is a habit worth adopting,
   and the same one each time: after writing a criterion, read it back literally
   against the requirement and ask whether it says the same thing.
3. SYSTEM_PROMPT is now exported solely so the test can assert it. That widens the
   module's public surface for a test's benefit, which the codebase already does
   elsewhere (buildPrompt, resolveOpenAiConfig, resolveAdminConfig) and which the
   comment labels. Consistent with existing practice rather than a new pattern.
4. Not this sprint's business, and now the fourth mention: the devteam2/sprint-11
   worktree and branch still exist.

WHAT NO GATE CAN ASSESS, and the sprint file is right to say so: whether the new
register is the wanted one. PRD v2 §1 states the output is not being judged, and tone
is not a property any gate here could evaluate even if it were. I can confirm the
prompt says what the sprint asked it to say, that nothing else about how the prompt is
built moved, and that the test will now catch any future change to it. Whether the
prose reads the way it should is the user's call, on two or three generated readings,
and if it has not landed the fix is another pass at this file rather than a defect
report.

Cleared to ship at dff8775. GroundTruth's second criterion is the one that matters:
the register changed and the grounding has to have held, checked on the
matchedYear: false path where events come from other years and fabrication would show
first.

CONDITIONAL: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 21, commit
dff8775ff3ef8ba53aa8d71796915fb89376a96b.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data
API via the anon client, 2026-08-23 ~06:03-06:06Z.
Four generations analysed: three on the matchedYear:false reading (1977-03-31) and
one on the matchedYear:true reading (1986-03-31).

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL. The grounding held completely -- no fabrication of any kind
in four generations, verified by computation against the supplied data rather than
by reading for plausibility. What did not hold reliably is year attribution on the
fallback path, which criterion 2 names explicitly and criterion 3 singles out as
the case that matters. One generation in three dated no event at all.

READ THIS FIRST SO THE VERDICT IS NOT MISREAD: this is not a fabrication finding.
Nothing unsupplied was ever asserted. The sprint's stated proof -- "the register
changed and the grounding held" -- is, on the evidence below, true.

CRITERION 1 -- generation still succeeds and persists, and a reload renders the
stored text. PASS.
  Four generations, all HTTP/2 303 back to the reading, 4010ms and comparable --
  the OpenAI-call range, not an error path. Each persisted: model
  gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, lengths 1044 / 751 / 905 / 975, horoscope_generated_at
  advancing each time, overwriting in place.
  Reload: a fresh GET of the 1986 reading renders the stored text.

CRITERION 2 -- the generated text still references only supplied data. The
grounding half PASSES, comprehensively. The year-attribution half is the finding.

  PLACEMENTS. Every body-in-sign claim across all four generations checked against
  that row's stored positions. Zero mismatches:
    1977 runs: Sun Aries, Moon Leo, Mercury Aries, Venus Aries (retrograde --
      stored retrograde true), Mars Pisces, Saturn Leo, Uranus Scorpio, Pluto Libra
    1986 run: Sun Aries, Saturn Sagittarius
  ASPECTS. Every aspect claim recomputed from the stored ecliptic longitudes
  against Sprint 12's orb table, and then checked against the supplied top-6 set
  (R4 supplies only the top 6, so an aspect that is real but outside that set would
  still be ungrounded):
    1977 supplied top-6, orb-ranked: Sun-Saturn trine 0.60, Saturn-Uranus square
      0.89, Mars-Uranus trine 2.05, Sun-Pluto opposition 2.23, Moon-Venus trine
      2.58, Saturn-Pluto sextile 2.83
    run 1 claimed: Sun-Saturn trine (0.60), Mars-Uranus trine (2.05), Sun-Pluto
      opposition (2.23) -- all valid, all inside the supplied six
    run 2 claimed: Sun-Saturn trine (0.60), Saturn-Uranus square (0.89) -- same
    run 3 claimed: Sun-Saturn trine (0.60), Mars-Uranus trine (2.05), Moon-Venus
      trine (2.58) -- same
    1986 run claimed: Sun-Saturn trine (orb 0.89), Jupiter-Saturn square (0.50),
      Moon-Uranus conjunction (0.87) -- all valid
  Not one invented aspect, and not one aspect drawn from outside the supplied set,
  in four generations.

  EVENT DETAIL -- R2's new grounding extension. I suspected a violation and it did
  not survive checking, which is worth recording because the near-miss is
  instructive. Run 1 says "the protests surrounding the Old National Library
  Building's closure in Singapore", and my first capture of the supplied event text
  was truncated at 80 characters and ended "...was closed to make way for a
  tunnel." On that partial text, "protests" looked invented. The full supplied
  string is "The Old National Library Building in Singapore was closed to make way
  for a tunnel, despite widespread protests." The protests are supplied.
  Same for the rest: "aimed to dismantle the existing power structure in Armenia"
  paraphrases the supplied "opening the 2018 Armenian revolution"; "communities
  felt a collective loss" paraphrases the supplied "deeply affecting the Latino
  community". No invented event detail in any run. I checked the full source text
  before reporting rather than filing a finding I would have had to withdraw.

CRITERION 3 -- the matchedYear:false path specifically. THIS IS WHERE THE FINDING
IS. I generated three times on it precisely because the sprint says this is where
fabrication would show first, and because temperature 0.9 means one sample proves
little.
  Supplied events for 1977-03-31 (matchedYear false): 2023 tornado/Belvidere, 2018
  Pashinyan, 2004 Singapore library, 1995 Selena, 1995 TAROM 371. None of them
  happened in 1977; the nearest is eighteen years later.
  Year attribution across the three runs:
    run 1: one of four events dated (Pashinyan, "in 2018"). The other three --
           Singapore, Selena, the tornado -- appear with no date.
    run 2: NO event dated at all. Years cited in the entire text: none.
    run 3: all four dated (1995, 2004, 2018, 2023).
  In no run was any event attributed to 1977. The explicit failure mode the
  criterion guards against -- narrating an event as happening on the reading's date
  -- never occurred, and I want that stated plainly.
  But run 2 reads, verbatim: "The Sun in Aries formed a trine with Saturn,
  contributing to a sense of focused determination. This resulted in significant
  protests, like Nikol Pashinyan's walk, as people sought to challenge authority
  and demand change." and "Mercury and Venus in Aries, alongside the Moon in Leo,
  amplified emotions surrounding loss and tragedy. The murder of Selena shocked the
  Latino community". A reader of that page has been told the 1977 sky produced
  these events and has been given no date for any of them. The reasonable inference
  is that they happened on the reading's date. They did not.
  The reader is misled by omission rather than by assertion. That is a narrower
  fault than fabrication and I am not calling it fabrication -- but the reader ends
  up believing the same false thing either way, which is what the criterion exists
  to prevent.
  Mitigating, and worth weighing: the page itself labels the section "No recorded
  event matched this exact year — showing notable happenings on this day across
  history instead." A careful reader has the correction available above the prose.
  Aggravating: this is a regression traceable to this sprint. Sprint 17's
  generation on this same reading dated every event it cited -- "Selena's tragic
  passing in 1995", "Pashinyan's revolutionary walk in 2018", "TAROM Flight 371 in
  1995 and the unfortunate concert collapse in 2023". The old effusive register
  carried the years; the new plain one drops them, inconsistently.

  The matchedYear:true path has no equivalent problem: the 1986 run cites no year,
  but its single supplied event (the Mexicana crash) genuinely did happen on
  1986-03-31, so there is nothing to misattribute. Grounding there was likewise
  clean.

WHY CONDITIONAL RATHER THAN PASS. Criterion 2 asks for "events attributed to their
own years". One run in three attributed none. On a sprint whose only live proof is
that the register changed without breaking grounding, that is not a clean pass, and
a PASS would put in the record that year attribution was verified when what I
actually observed was that it varies.
WHY CONDITIONAL RATHER THAN FAIL. Nothing was fabricated. Every placement, every
aspect and every event detail across four generations came from the supplied data.
The astrological grounding this sprint risked is intact, and the fix is a prompt
line rather than a defect hunt -- the sprint file already anticipates that shape of
fix ("the fix is another pass at the same file, not a defect report").

WHAT WOULD CLEAR IT. A prompt rule requiring each cited event to carry its year
whenever matchedYear is false, then reship. I will re-test by generating three or
more times on the same 1977 reading and checking that every cited event is dated in
every run -- one sample cannot settle a temperature-0.9 behaviour, which is why
this finding took three.

TEST DATA. No new rows. Running count of rows this role has left in production
remains eleven. Four OpenAI generations billed. Both readings used are left holding
valid generated horoscopes, not probe state.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks
are curl over HTTPS against production plus direct anon calls to the Supabase Data
API. Whether the new register is the wanted one is explicitly the user's judgement,
not this gate's -- PRD v2 §1 says the output is not being judged, and tone is not a
property I could assess anyway. Everything above is about grounding, which is
checkable, not about whether the writing is good.

FAIL: GroundTruth live test round 2, Sprint 21, commit
db915b8616bc0bcbdf2645588eab256b5c262cf3.
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, the production Supabase Data API
via the anon client, and NASA JPL Horizons as an independent reference.
2026-08-23 ~06:27-06:32Z. Four generations on the matchedYear:false reading
(1977-03-31).

VERDICT: FAIL. The round-1 fix worked for its stated goal and introduced a worse
problem in its place. Every cited event now carries its year -- that part is
solved, verified across four runs. But in three of those four runs the model dates
the ASPECT to the event's year, asserting specific planetary positions for dates
where no data was supplied. Those assertions are checkable, and they are false.

WHAT THE FIX ACHIEVED. Round 1's finding is closed. Across four generations, every
event mentioned carried its own year within the same sentence or the one adjoining
it: 2023 tornado, 2018 Pashinyan, 2004 Singapore library, 1995 Selena, 1995 TAROM.
No run omitted a date the way round 1's run 2 did. The unconditional year rule does
what it was written to do.

WHAT IT BROKE. The rule pushed a year into sentences that also describe the sky,
and the model attached it to the wrong half. Verbatim, from three separate runs:

  run 2: "On March 31, 1995, Saturn in Leo squared Uranus in Scorpio as Selena was
          murdered."
  run 1: "In 2004, Saturn squared Uranus while the Old National Library was closed
          for a tunnel project."
  run 3: "In 2018, Mars in Pisces trine Uranus coincided with Nikol Pashinyan
          beginning his protest walk."
  run 2: "On March 31, 2004, the Moon in Leo trined Venus in Aries while the Old
          National Library Building faced closure."
  run 2: "In the same year, Pluto in Libra was in opposition to the Sun in Aries
          when TAROM Flight 371 crashed."

Each of these states that a supplied aspect obtained on a date that is not the
reading's date. The supplied data covers 1977-03-31 and nothing else. The sky on
1995-03-31, 2004-03-31 and 2018-03-31 is not in the payload in any form, so every
one of these sentences asserts something the model was never given.

THEY ARE ALSO FALSE. I did not stop at "unsupplied" -- I checked them against NASA
JPL Horizons, geocentric ecliptic-of-date, the same reference I have used since
Sprint 6:

  Claim (run 2): Saturn in Leo, square Uranus in Scorpio, on 1995-03-31.
  Actual:  Saturn was in PISCES 18.09. Uranus was in CAPRICORN 29.97.
           Separation 48.12 degrees -- not a square, not within any orb of one.
           Both signs wrong, and the aspect does not exist.

  Claim (run 1): Saturn squared Uranus in 2004 (2004-03-31).
  Actual:  Saturn CANCER 6.81, Uranus PISCES 4.89, separation 121.92 degrees.
           That is nearer a trine than a square. The claimed aspect is not there.

  For reference, the supplied 1977-03-31 values these were lifted from: Saturn Leo
  10.05, Uranus Scorpio 10.95, separation 90.89 -- a genuine square with orb 0.89,
  and second in the supplied top-6. The model took a real aspect from the reading's
  own sky and re-dated it to somebody else's.

This is the failure mode this sprint exists to prevent, and it is a harder version
of it than round 1's. Round 1 misled by omission -- an undated event a reader might
place on the wrong day. Round 2 misleads by assertion: a specific, confident,
falsifiable statement about where two planets stood on a named date. A reader who
checks will find it wrong.

GROUNDING THAT DID HOLD, so the fix is targeted rather than a rewrite:
  - Placements against the reading's own date: every "X in Sign" claim across all
    four runs matches the stored positions. Zero mismatches. Run 4 additionally
    cites exact degrees -- Sun 10.66, Saturn 10.05, Uranus 10.95, Mars 8.90 -- and
    all four match the stored values to two decimals, which is R4's rounding rule
    working.
  - Aspects as aspects: every aspect named is real for 1977-03-31 and inside the
    supplied top-6 (Sun-Saturn trine 0.60, Saturn-Uranus square 0.89, Mars-Uranus
    trine 2.05, Sun-Pluto opposition 2.23, Moon-Venus trine 2.58, Saturn-Pluto
    sextile 2.83). Not one invented aspect, not one drawn from outside the set.
  - Event detail: no invention. Every detail traces to the supplied text.
  The defect is exclusively in which DATE the aspects are attached to.

RUN 4 SHOWS THE CORRECT SHAPE, which is worth recording because it means the prompt
is close rather than wrong:
  "Sun in Aries at 10.66° trined Saturn in Leo at 10.05° on March 31, 1977. ... The
   recent tornado collapse at a concert in Belvidere, Illinois in 2023 reflects an
   imbalance in the powerful energy present during this time."
  The aspect is dated to the reading's date; the event is dated to its own year;
  the connection between them is made without claiming they share a sky. One run in
  four got there unprompted.

WHAT WOULD CLEAR THIS. The year rule needs to be scoped to events only, plus an
explicit statement that the supplied positions describe the reading's date alone
and must never be asserted for any other date. Run 4 is the target register and it
already exists in the model's output, so this reads as a prompt-precision problem
rather than a capability one.
  On re-test I will generate at least four times again and check both properties
  together: every event dated to its own year AND no planetary claim attached to
  any date other than the reading's. Round 1 taught me that one sample cannot
  settle a temperature-0.9 behaviour; round 2 taught me that fixing one half can
  break the other, so both need checking in the same pass.

CRITERION 1 -- generation still succeeds and persists, and a reload renders the
stored text. PASS, unaffected. Four generations, all 303, lengths 907 / 871 / 924 /
793, model gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, horoscope_generated_at advancing, overwriting in
place.

CRITERION 3 -- the matchedYear:false path specifically. This is where I tested, and
it is where the defect lives. Four runs, three affected.

TEST DATA. No new rows; the count this role has left in production remains eleven.
Four OpenAI generations billed this round. The 1977 reading currently holds run 4's
text, which is the clean one.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension. All checks are curl over
HTTPS against production, direct anon calls to the Supabase Data API, and the JPL
Horizons HTTP API as reference. Whether the register itself is the wanted one
remains the user's judgement, not this gate's; nothing above is a comment on the
writing.

FAIL: GroundTruth live test round 3, Sprint 21, commit
db915b8616bc0bcbdf2645588eab256b5c262cf3 (unchanged since round 2 -- no reship;
this is a re-test against the amended acceptance criteria).
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, the production Supabase Data API
via the anon client, and NASA JPL Horizons as reference. 2026-08-23 ~06:40Z.
Five fresh generations on the matchedYear:false reading (1977-03-31).

VERDICT: FAIL. The amendment is present, anchored, and I have honoured it: year
attribution is withdrawn and I am not gating on it. But the amendment withdrew one
clause of criterion 2 and left the rest standing, and the rest is what fails.

AMENDMENT VERIFIED FIRST, as it asks. Present in the sprint file, dated 23 Aug
2026, explicitly withdrawing "events attributed to their own years rather than
narrated as happening on the reading's date", recording the defect rather than
deleting it, and giving reasoning and a follow-up note. It is a real amendment with
a stated rationale, not a quiet deletion. I have tested accordingly and year
attribution appears nowhere in this verdict.

WHAT STILL STANDS IN CRITERION 2. The withdrawal covers the events clause only. The
surviving text reads: "The generated text still references only supplied data --
placements that appear in the stored positions, aspects within the supplied set."
That is the clause this build fails.

THE DEFECT, IN FIVE OF FIVE RUNS. The model asserts the reading's planetary
configuration as obtaining on other dates. The supplied payload describes
1977-03-31 and nothing else; the sky of 1995, 2004, 2018 and 2023 is not in it in
any form. Sixteen sentences across five runs. Verbatim samples:

  run 1: "On March 31, 1995, the Sun opposed Pluto."
         "During the same day in 1995, Saturn squared Uranus."
         "By March 31, 2004, the Sun trine Saturn suggested a clash between
          authority and change..."
  run 2: "The Moon in Leo trined Venus in Aries on March 31, 2004."
  run 3: "In 2018, Uranus was prominent as Nikol Pashinyan's protest walk began..."
  run 4: "On March 31, 2018, Mercury in Aries fueled protests..."
  run 5: "In 2004, Saturn squared Uranus during the protests over the Old National
          Library Building in Singapore."

  Every single run contains a variant of "On March 31, 1995, the Sun opposed
  Pluto." Five for five.

CHECKED AGAINST JPL HORIZONS, not asserted:
  1995-03-31: Sun Aries 10.31, Pluto Sagittarius 0.40. Separation 129.91 degrees.
    An opposition requires 180 +/- 8. The claim is FALSE -- and it is the one
    sentence that appears in all five generations.
  1995-03-31: Saturn Pisces 18.09, Uranus Capricorn 29.97, separation 48.12. The
    claimed square is FALSE. (Carried from round 2, re-confirmed.)
  2004-03-31: Saturn Cancer 6.81, Uranus Pisces 4.89, separation 121.92. The
    claimed square is FALSE. (Carried from round 2.)
  2018-03-31: Mercury Aries 12.96. The claim "Mercury in Aries" is COINCIDENTALLY
    TRUE.
  2023-03-31: Moon Leo 6.66. The claim "Moon in Leo" is COINCIDENTALLY TRUE.
  So the output is a mix of false statements and accidentally correct ones. All of
  them are ungrounded in the same way -- asserted about dates for which the model
  was given no data -- and the two that happen to be right are right by luck, which
  is not a property anyone can rely on.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE DEFECT THAT WAS WITHDRAWN. The amendment describes the fault
as "misleading *by omission*" and states, of round 1, "Nothing was fabricated in
any run -- no event was ever attributed to 1977, and every placement and aspect
traced to the stored payload." That was accurate for round 1 at commit dff8775 and
I stand behind it; it is what I recorded.
  It is not accurate for the shipped build. At db915b8 the failure is the opposite
  shape: not a missing date, but an asserted one. "On March 31, 1995, the Sun
  opposed Pluto" is a placement that does not appear in the stored positions,
  stated as fact, and false. A reader is not left to infer something wrong -- they
  are told something wrong.
  The amendment notes round 2 failed and concludes "the behaviour is not reliably
  fixable by a prompt line", which reads as though round 2 failed for the same
  reason round 1 did. It did not. Round 2's notes recorded the cross-date
  assertions and the JPL falsification; that finding is not reflected in the
  amendment's account, and the amendment's stated basis for acceptance -- "the
  register changed and the grounding held ... Zero fabrications" -- is contradicted
  by what the current build does five times out of five.
  I am not asserting the amendment was written in bad faith. It reads like it was
  drafted from round 1's findings. I am flagging that its factual account and the
  deployed behaviour disagree, because that gap is exactly what an amendment is
  supposed to prevent.

WHAT DID HOLD, so the remaining fix is narrow:
  - Placements attributed to the reading's own date: correct in every run, matching
    the stored positions.
  - Aspects, taken as aspects: every one named is real for 1977-03-31 and inside
    the supplied top-6 (Sun-Saturn trine 0.60, Saturn-Uranus square 0.89,
    Mars-Uranus trine 2.05, Sun-Pluto opposition 2.23, Moon-Venus trine 2.58,
    Saturn-Pluto sextile 2.83). Nothing invented.
  - Event detail: still no invention; details trace to supplied strings.
  The whole defect is the date each aspect is attached to. Round 2's run 4 showed
  the correct shape unprompted -- aspect dated to 1977, event dated to its own year
  -- so the register can produce it.

CRITERION 1 -- generation succeeds and persists, reload renders stored text. PASS,
unaffected. Five generations, lengths 890 / 892 / 1122 / 829 / 944, all persisted
and overwriting in place.

WHAT I NEED IN ORDER TO PASS THIS. One of two things, and the choice is the user's,
not mine:
  (a) A fix: the prompt must state that the supplied positions describe the
      reading's date alone and must never be asserted for any other date. I will
      re-test across at least five generations and check the same detector.
  (b) An explicit decision to accept and defer THIS defect too, recorded the way
      the year-attribution one was -- naming it as false cross-date astronomical
      assertions rather than as omission, so the record says what was actually
      accepted. If that is the call, say so and I will record a verdict against it
      without further argument.
  What I will not do is record a PASS whose notes say the grounding held, when five
  runs out of five say otherwise. That is the one thing a gate cannot do and remain
  worth having.

TEST DATA. No new rows; the count remains eleven. Five OpenAI generations billed
this round, thirteen across the sprint.

TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension. curl over HTTPS, direct anon
Data API calls, and the JPL Horizons HTTP API. Whether the register is the wanted
one remains the user's judgement; nothing here comments on the writing.

PASS: GroundTruth live test round 4, Sprint 21, commit
db915b8616bc0bcbdf2645588eab256b5c262cf3 (unchanged; no reship since round 2 --
this is a verdict against the corrected acceptance criteria, not against new code).
Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data
API via the anon client, 2026-08-23 ~06:48Z.

VERDICT: PASS, against acceptance criteria from which both grounding clauses have
been explicitly withdrawn. Read the scope section before reading the verdict. This

WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT COVER, stated at length because the gap is large and a
one-line verdict would misrepresent it.
  The deployed application asserts astronomically false statements to its users. In
  five generations out of five on the matchedYear:false path, it attaches the
  reading's planetary configuration to dates that configuration did not describe:
    "On March 31, 1995, the Sun opposed Pluto." -- present in all five runs. JPL:
      Sun Aries 10.31, Pluto Sagittarius 0.40, separation 129.91 degrees. There is
      no opposition. The statement is false.
    "In 2004, Saturn squared Uranus" -- JPL separation 121.92 degrees. False.
    "Saturn in Leo squared Uranus in Scorpio" on 1995-03-31 -- JPL: Saturn Pisces
      18.09, Uranus Capricorn 29.97, separation 48.12. Both signs wrong, no square.
      False.
    Two further claims, Mercury in Aries in 2018 and Moon in Leo in 2023, happen to
    be true. They are true by coincidence and are ungrounded in exactly the same
    way as the false ones.
  This is not fabrication of placements -- every placement is real for the reading's
  own date, every aspect is real and inside the supplied top-6 set, and no event
  detail is invented. The entire defect is which date each aspect is attached to.
  It is accepted and deferred to a data-quality epic by the user's decision, named
  there as "The app asserts astronomically false statements", which is the accurate
  name for it.
